note: Both overstated claims bounded, and one turned out to be false in code as well as in prose. (1) The 'small model + large datastore matches a much bigger model' line is now attributed to the kNN-LM literature and explicitly marked 'not a measurement of this implementation... a mechanism, not a capability', since nothing here benchmarks against a larger model. (2) 'generation never degrades below the raw model' claimed more than fail-open delivers; the docstring now separates What IS guaranteed (no neighbours above the gate / lambda~0 / any exception -> lm_probs returned UNCHANGED) from What is NOT guaranteed (a blend that fires can be wrong — the similarity gate exists because confidently-recalled neighbours from another fact once outvoted the exact match). (3) Found while testing the narrow claim: it was not actually true. The except list stopped at TypeError/ValueError/KeyError/AttributeError/ZeroDivisionError/FloatingPointError, so a RuntimeError/OSError/IndexError/OverflowError/MemoryError from a FAISS- or numpy-backed query escaped into the token loop and killed the generation the contract exists to protect. note: Replaced floor-stride pooling with np.array_split over the whole vector, so all 64 buckets together cover every element regardless of divisibility. Measured before/after: size 200 covered 192 (8 neurons dropped on every call), size 1000 covered 960 (40 dropped); both now cover 100%, and a change confined to the previously-dropped tail now moves the output where it used to be invisible. Sizes divisible by 64 were always correct and are pinned unchanged. Also corrected the comment: it said 'hash-project', which is a different operation with different collision behaviour — it is contiguous mean-pooling, and the comment now says so. note: Merge identity no longer trusts a caller-supplied id alone. seen_events maps event_id -> the content fingerprint (stage, method, reasons, deterministic, before/after chars, before/after sha256) it was first seen with. Same id + same content = the copied-receipt duplicate this dedupe exists for, still dropped. Same id + DIFFERENT content = a collision: the entry is kept under its content identity and a degradation is recorded, because losing a real mutation from a user-facing-answer audit trail is worse than carrying a redundant one. A differing after_sha256 alone is enough to keep both. Legacy (no-id) entries keep their existing content-tuple identity, minus the sequence number that varies by position. Tests: tests/test_mutation_ledger_survives_id_collisions.py (10).
title: Caller-controlled event IDs can suppress distinct mutations

note: Caps kept (a live belief graph should not get an unbounded logging sweep) but the result now states its own completeness. AuditReport gains contradiction_scan_considered/_total/_truncated, contradiction_reporting_capped, a coverage fraction and contradiction_result_is_complete; __str__ appends '[partial scan: N/M beliefs]' so a truncated audit can no longer read identically to a clean one. Also added the missing ordering guarantee: eligible beliefs are sorted by id before truncation, so the examined subset is deterministic — previously the truncation was arbitrarily partial and a contradiction could appear and vanish between audits with no change to the beliefs. note: All three parts. (1) Deadline: the model call runs under asyncio.wait_for with DELIBERATION_TIMEOUT_S=45s (per-call override via deliberation_timeout_s), so a wedged model can no longer stall the decision and everything waiting on it. (2) Typed fallback: TimeoutError and provider errors (RuntimeError/AttributeError/TypeError/ValueError/OSError) are caught and turned into a Decision carrying metadata.degraded, deliberated=False, confidence 0.0 and an explaining reason — asyncio.CancelledError is deliberately re-raised, since cancellation is the caller's decision. This matters because _parse falls back to actions[0], so a failed deliberation previously returned a well-formed Decision naming a real action, indistinguishable from a considered choice. (3) Silent downgrade: when _native_system2_deliberate returns None the drop to the weaker ordinary route is recorded as metadata.native_system2_declined and in the trace. Tests: tests/test_deliberation_is_bounded_and_receipted.py (10).
title: Ordinary generation has no deadline or typed fallback

note: Replay now rebuilds each queued record (_replay_record returns None for an unknown kind rather than crashing the sweep), computes its hash_key, skips it when _is_duplicate says it already committed, and calls _mark_committed on success — the first commit path already did all of this and replay did none of it. Site: finetune quality. Belief confidence: a NaN belief won the top-5 prompt injection outright. Scheduler: a NaN interval passed '< 0' validation then made 'now-last_run >= interval' False forever (registered, healthy, never ran) — zero is KEPT as 'every tick', which is bounded by the scheduler cadence and relied on by the suite. Volition: NaN inquiry score sorted as highest priority (already fixed in-place, verified). Timeout: bounded to (0,600] at a subprocess boundary. Quality: NaN skipped the heuristic fallback AND became the stored score that rotation sorts on. Reliability: one NaN-reporting service made the whole global stability mean NaN.
